A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ToMAP study. The complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and matchable, including material relocated into v3's new Appendix G.

before.justification: v2 reports original persuasion experiments, ablations, ToM predictor evaluations and a human assessment of 50 conversations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds another persuader backbone, additional persuadee evaluations, long-CoT controls and a 100-conversation human assessment.

M1.justification: The counterclaim predictor, BGE-M3/MLP attitude predictor, prompt augmentation, PPO rewards and Appendix C pipeline are retained. Applying the framework to LLaMa3.2 does not introduce a different method component or procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions train on CMV and evaluate the same claim-persuasion task on CMV, Anthropic and args.me. The added backbones and persuadees change model configurations within this coverage; the larger human assessment changes sample size.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 add a long-CoT prompting comparator. Table 1 also includes LLaMa3.2-3B base, SFT and RL counterparts. Existing larger-LLM baselines and ToM ablation comparators remain; newly cited systems such as TreeDebater are not evaluated.

E3.justification: v3 substantially expands model settings: it trains LLaMa3.2-3B alongside Qwen2.5-3B and evaluates against Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B and GPT-4o-mini. It introduces long-CoT prompting controls and increases human validation from 10 to 20 conversations per attitude level, totaling 100 instead of 50. Existing dataset splits, metrics and PPO settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new long-CoT comparisons test whether encouraging longer reasoning can explain the persuasion gains without ToMAP. The human-alignment analysis is expanded. Existing attitude-predictor ablations, training trajectories, ten-turn analysis, strategy analysis and appendix case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over three evaluation trials and use accuracy and Cohen's kappa for human alignment. No new seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures appear. The changed human sample size and agreement values belong to E3 and E6.

E6.justification: Original Table 1 scores are retained, while v3 adds substantial results for LLaMa3.2, additional persuadees and long-CoT controls. LLaMa3.2-ToMAP reports a 24.35 average versus 21.76 for its RL counterpart. The enlarged human study reports accuracy/kappa of 0.78/0.725 instead of 0.76/0.70, using a different sample size. Some new aggregates are inconsistent: Table 11's ToMAP scores average approximately 11.44, but its Avg. column reports 11.77.

T1.justification: The agreement-score definition, normalized reward, PPO objective and ToM formulations in Equations 1–11 are mathematically unchanged. v3 adds an intuitive explanation of Equation 3 and standardizes q/Q notation, without adding formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 modestly narrows the human-cognition framing: the introduction describes inspiration from human ToM instead of simulating it, and the conclusion drops the goal of more human-like persuaders. The central two-module RL contribution and the abstract's 39.4% relative gain over GPT-4o remain.

C2.justification: v3 argues that adversarial persuasion calls for implicit ToM, interprets the long-CoT controls as showing limited benefit from longer thinking alone, and adds an interpretation of transfer to larger persuadees in Section 5.5. Existing explanations of diversity, long-conversation gains, computational constraints and misuse risks are retained.

D1.justification: v3 removes the reproducibility statement asserting that the full codebase is included in supplementary material. The abstract's GitHub link and the appendix prompts, pseudocode, hyperparameters, hardware and timing details remain. This changes access disclosure without establishing that code availability itself changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning beyond ToM evaluation to explicit versus implicit enhancement methods, covering Bayesian planning, simulation and agentic finetuning and locating ToMAP within this literature. It also adds TreeDebater, Debate-to-Write, AI-Realtor and application references. Frith and Frith (2005) is omitted.

P1.justification: v3 shortens the abstract, edits terminology and selected explanations, expands the human-study description, and adds Section 5.5 and Appendix G. It renames the ethical statement to Impact Statement and removes the reproducibility and LLM-usage statements. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch to a two-column conference layout. Table 1 is reorganized by backbone, Tables 2–3 gain rows, and Table 11 is added. The updated human confusion matrix moves from main-text Figure 3 to appendix Figure 6; the other figures are retained but resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: The second backbone and additional persuadees better support generalization, while the long-CoT control and expanded human assessment strengthen validation. These benefits are limited by new reporting inconsistencies: Table 11's ToMAP scores average 11.44 rather than 11.77, and Table 2 reports Qwen long-CoT at 8.73 whereas Table 3 implies 9.39, without explaining a setting difference. The individual results still support broader effectiveness, yielding a modest net improvement despite these defects.
